# axiolid-overlay

Deterministic validated planar overlay contract.

## Overview

Validated, deterministic planar booleans (intersection, union, difference, xor) and offsets over regions with holes, plus the planar operations built on them: arc-aware booleans and arrangements, polyline strokes, Minkowski morphology bounds, minimum enclosing circles and rectangles, visibility, and exact intersection of many segments by a sweep. Inputs are validated and refused with a typed error rather than repaired. It answers a query and keeps no structure; editable subdivisions with persistent identity live in `axiolid-arrangement`.

## Design notes

- Straight-edged booleans (`Region`, `overlay`, `union_soup`) and arc-aware ones (`arc_overlay`,
  `ArcArrangement`) share one exact core in `src/exact_arc.rs` (ADR 0070, #173): every
  topological decision is an exact sign, and output is rounded once, so an input vertex comes
  back bit-identical. `i_overlay` remains only for offsets. The core's maintenance rules and
  verification commands are in that module's docs.
- An arc polygon is checked exactly for self-contact, shared boundary and hole nesting by
  `check_arc_polygon`, with no tolerance in any contact or nesting decision (`src/arc_check.rs`,
  #352, ADR 0095). `scripts/probe_arc_check_mutants.py` lists the faults its tests must catch.
  `check_arc_polygon_with` can also report edges that miss each other by less than a distance
  (`ArcCheckOptions::with_clearance`, `src/arc_clearance.rs`, #388), decided exactly; its faults
  are listed by `scripts/probe_arc_clearance_mutants.py`.
- Operand validation and output settling share one exact notion of when two boundary edges
  meet (`src/contact.rs`, #272): an end on the other edge within the tolerance, or a proper
  crossing, so every output is a valid operand wherever it lies.
  `scripts/probe_edge_contact_mutants.py` lists the faults its tests must catch.
- A soup of convex parts fanned into triangles reduces to the parts' outlines even where the
  parts overlap and share vertices: the chain is reduced group by group when one walk through it
  closes a crossing cycle. Edges given more than once, and edges meeting at a shared vertex, are
  not paired again for every copy, so a soup whose grown parts line up costs about what its
  outlines cost (#338). `overlay_within` and `union_soup_within` take `ExecutionOptions`: with a
  memory budget the subdivision is charged before it allocates and refused with
  `OverlayRefusal::BudgetExceeded` before it would hold more (`src/budget.rs`, ADR 0088).
  `scripts/probe_grown_soup_mutants.py` lists the faults its tests must catch.
- Ring validation asks the crate's box tree for the edge pairs that can meet within the
  tolerance, decided by the same exact test in the same order, so a ring of 100,000 corners
  validates in about `n log n`. A `Region` carries the proof that its rings are valid under its
  tolerance, set only by `Region::new` and by settled outputs, and booleans on regions under that
  tolerance do not validate them again (#341). `scripts/probe_ring_validation_mutants.py` lists
  the faults its tests must catch.
- `Region::new` also refuses rings that cross into each other (`src/nesting.rs`, ADR 0104,
  #448): a hole outside its outer ring (`HoleOutsideOuter`), two holes of a polygon that
  overlap (`HolesOverlap`), two polygons that overlap (`PolygonsOverlap`). The decision is exact
  and tolerance-free, on one arrangement of all rings; rings may touch at points or share a
  stretch with the polygons' insides on opposite sides, as settled outputs do. Operations do not
  re-check their outputs. `scripts/probe_region_nesting_mutants.py` lists the faults its tests
  must catch.
- `free_faces` returns the bounded faces of the plane that obstacle polygons and barriers leave
  free, each ring edge with the inputs it lies on, and `FreeFaces::locate` says which face a
  point is in (`src/free_faces.rs`, #490, ADR 0109). A gap narrower than the closing width is
  closed by a reported bridge, never by moving an input, and a free region narrower than the
  width is a closed gap, listed apart. It runs on `axiolid-exact-arrangement`, so every decision is
  an exact sign and the rings are snap-rounded as the visible faces are (ADR 0100).
  `scripts/probe_free_faces_mutants.py` lists the faults its tests must catch.
- A degenerate input ring refuses the operation by default. `overlay_with` and
  `union_soup_with` with `OverlayOptions::dropping_degenerate_rings` leave out a ring that
  is too short, has a repeated vertex, or has zero area under the exact `ZeroArea` rule,
  and report each one with its place, reason and area (`src/degenerate.rs`, #256). A
  self-intersecting ring is never dropped. `scripts/probe_degenerate_drop_mutants.py` lists
  the faults its tests must catch.
- `segment_intersections` (`src/segment_sweep.rs`, #146) is a Bentley-Ottmann sweep over
  many segments with its own exact rational points; its reporting rule and degeneracy
  handling are in that module's docs, and `scripts/probe_segment_sweep_mutants.py` lists
  the faults its tests must catch.
- Minkowski sums and erosions take one hull per boundary edge. Exactly collinear corners
  are merged first, and a chord proved exactly to lie in the summed set trims the hulls it
  spans to what its own hull does not hold, so a wall of many short edges costs about its
  teeth, not their square, and the union stays the same set (`src/cover.rs`, #323).
  A chord whose hull or any trimmed hull would be a ring of zero area is not used, so
  trimming never adds a ring the arrangement refuses (#331). `scripts/probe_minkowski_cover_mutants.py`
  and `scripts/probe_minkowski_degenerate_mutants.py` list the faults its tests must catch.
- The disc morphology has two modes (`MorphologyMode`, ADR 0087, #330). `Exact`, the
  default and the behaviour of `erode_inner` and its siblings, is bit for bit the route
  above; a CAD kernel takes it. Its cost still grows with the square of the corners where
  teeth stand closer than their tips' slivers are wide. `Fast`, through
  `erode_inner_with` and its siblings, first fills the summed set's notches with chords
  proved to lie outside it, each used only when the excess it adds is within the caller's
  budget, and keeps the inner or outer side: the excess goes into `MorphologyBound`'s
  deviation and is reported by `Region::excess`. A wall of teeth then costs about its
  corners; a rule engine takes it (`src/fill.rs`). It fills needles deeper than the
  disc too, each bounded by its own slab (#428).
  `scripts/probe_fast_morphology_mutants.py` lists the faults its tests must catch.

## Changes

Latest release, 0.4.0 (2026-11-13):

### Changed

- **Breaking:** `OverlayError` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and gains
  `HolesOverlap` and `PolygonsOverlap`, which `Region::new` returns; a
  `match` on it needs a wildcard arm. `HoleOutsideOuter` now also names a
  hole that crosses its outer ring. `Region::translate` checks its result as
  `Region::new` does, since rounding each vertex can turn a contact into a
  crossing; `Region::sweep` moves its copy unchecked, since the copy only
  feeds `union`, and returns what it did before (#448, ADR 0104).

### Fixed

- `MorphologyMode::Fast` fills a needle notch deeper than the disc. A wall of
  needles 0.25 m deep under a disc of radius 0.4 m kept every notch, since no
  chord was proposed over a notch deeper than `t`: #340's room with a column
  and 124 such needles gave 562 corners, 500 needles 2,066, both as `Exact`. Proposals now also pass `t` over a needle no wider
  than `needle_width(t, budget) = 2 sqrt(2 t budget + budget^2)` whose
  vertices project inside its mouth, and across a vertex exactly on the chord.
  The bound of a notch deeper than `t` is the widest of its pieces between the
  vertices exactly on the chord, one needle's (2.5e-8 for a 2 cm fixture)
  instead of the whole wall's (2.5e-4), and a deep chord over the budget is
  split at its on-line vertex nearest the middle. The 124 needles give 68
  corners for a dilation and 72 for an erosion, and the 2,002 and
  10,002 corner walls of `benches/disc_erosion.rs` (`deep`) in 0.014 to
  0.017 s and 0.07 s, where main takes 4.4 to 5.0 s at 2,002 corners. The side, the stated deviation and `Exact` are
  unchanged, and the 30 cases of #330, #340 and #345 in that bench give the
  same results bit for bit. A wall whose valleys are collinear only up to
  rounding keeps them (#483). `src/fill.rs`, `src/cover.rs`, ADR 0087 (#428);
  `scripts/probe_fast_morphology_mutants.py` lists the faults its tests must
  catch.
- `Region::new` refuses a polygon set whose rings cross into each other:
  part of a hole outside its own outer ring (`HoleOutsideOuter`), two holes
  of one polygon that cross, nest or repeat (`HolesOverlap`), and a point in
  two polygons (`PolygonsOverlap`). It accepted them, and the operations read
  such a set three ways: the fast morphology's notch fill took a hole's
  needles beyond its outer ring for the set's boundary. On #345's fuzz seed
  21351 (needles at y = 2.2955 past the outer ring's top edge at 2.1202)
  `dilate_outer_with(0.9046, fast(1e-2))` left out (2.0172, 3.0256), 0.8993
  from the region, with a stated deviation of 4.7e-3. The check is exact, with
  no tolerance, on one arrangement of all rings. Rings may still touch at
  points and share a stretch where their insides lie on opposite sides, which
  settled outputs do. A region of one ring costs what it did. `Region::new` of
  a floor of 100,000 corners with 200 holes takes 0.34 s instead of 0.083 s
  (10,000 corners: 0.032 s instead of 0.007 s;
  `benches/ring_validation.rs`, case `holes`). `overlay` and `union_soup`
  operands are unchanged. `src/nesting.rs`;
  `scripts/probe_region_nesting_mutants.py` lists the faults its tests must
  catch (#448, ADR 0104).

- The exact arrangement finds the carriers of a piece among the edges that
  cover it, not among every edge sharing some stretch with its edge. An edge
  that many others stand on cost the square of their number: 1,000 rooms
  standing on one corridor edge took 2.2 s, 2,000 took 8.6 s and 4,000 took
  35 s in `Region::new`, and a rectangle with 1,000 holes standing on its
  bottom edge took 5.3 s, 2,000 took 19.7 s and 4,000 took 87 s. They now
  take 0.05 s and 0.22 s (corridor, 1,000 and 4,000) and 0.05 s and 0.23 s
  (holes). The arrangement is unchanged bit for bit
  (`benches/ring_validation.rs`, cases `corridor` and `bays`, #448).

- `MorphologyMode::Fast` fills the walls of a floor with sub-budget teeth
  in bounded time and memory. On #345's 3 m floor (teeth 0.5 mm deep, 1 mm
  budget) the chord over the room's corner, too deep for the budget, was
  split at the corner, and the chord left, from the corner along the wall,
  ended at a valley instead of a tip: not proved, it was split down to
  single edges, so thousands of teeth stayed and the sum kept their
  quadratic cost (an inner erosion by 1.4 m took 13 s and 0.86 GB at
  10,000 corners, 71 s and 4.8 GB at 20,000, over 20 GB at 50,000). A chord
  not proved is now tried without its start edge, its end edge, or both,
  before it is split. The results are unchanged bit for bit, the excess is still
  within the budget and reported, `Exact` is unchanged. Release, median of
  5, inner erosion, r = 1.4 m: 0.078 s and 6 MB at 10,000 corners, 0.39 s
  and 15 MB at 50,000, 0.77 s and 25 MB at 100,000, 1.57 s and 48 MB at
  200,000, with the same for 1.49 m and 1.6 m
  (`tools/benchmark/benches/disc_erosion.rs`, walls `floor`;
  `docs/research/fast-morphology-on-toothed-floors.md`; `src/fill.rs`,
  #345, ADR 0087). `scripts/probe_fast_morphology_mutants.py` lists the
  faults its tests must catch.
